leaders.priorTitle: Provost and Vice President for Academic Affairs
leaders.nextRole: Chancellor of the Southern Illinois University system
leaders.notes: Ninth president; his first day was February 1, 1991. His tenure defined MTSU's rapid 1990s growth, including the University Honors College and a new library later named the James E. Walker Library. Left in 2000 to lead the SIU system.

leaders.priorTitle: Longtime MTSU administrator and faculty member (MTSU alumnus)
leaders.nextRole: Returned to Middle Tennessee State University
leaders.notes: Named interim president by the Tennessee Board of Regents; served October 2000 to August 2001, becoming the second MTSU alumnus to lead the institution, bridging the Walker-to-McPhee transition.

leaders.priorTitle: Executive Vice Chancellor, Chief Academic Officer and interim Chancellor
leaders.notes: Tenth president, selected August 2001; oversaw more than $400 million in campus improvements. On March 17, 2026 he announced he will step down as president effective December 2026, triggering an MTSU presidential search; he remains the sitting president.

leaders.priorTitle: Dean of the School of Business Administration
leaders.notes: Seventh president; led Montclair from state college to university status in 1994. Left in 1997 to become the first African American president of Wayne State University. Montclair's Science Hall was renamed Irvin D. Reid Hall in 2023.

leaders.nextRole: Returned to Montclair State faculty; later Director of the University Honors Program; retired 2017
leaders.notes: Served as acting president in the interim between Reid's 1997 departure and Cole's 1998 arrival. A 33-year Montclair employee in faculty and administrative roles; later elected chair of the New Jersey Council for the Humanities.
Eighth president and first woman to lead Montclair; served 23 years (September 1998 to July 2021), nearly doubling enrollment to more than 21,000 students and elevating the university to R2 status.

leaders.priorTitle: Dean of the Watts College of Public Service and Community Solutions and Vice Provost for Public Service and Social Impact
leaders.notes: Ninth president; assumed office August 2, 2021. At Arizona State he led the nation's largest comprehensive public affairs college.

leaders.priorTitle: Assistant to the President of the University System of Maryland (earlier senior administrator at University of Maryland Eastern Shore)
leaders.notes: Ninth president; his 26-year tenure (1984-2010), known as the Morgan Renaissance, brought unprecedented growth and national prominence. Died September 11, 2025 at age 81.

leaders.priorTitle: Chancellor of the University of Wisconsin Colleges and University of Wisconsin-Extension
leaders.notes: Tenth president; assumed office July 1, 2010 and has led Morgan for more than 15 years, guiding its rise to R2 doctoral-research status and a major campus expansion. No successor search announced.

university: North Carolina Agricultural and Technical State University

leaders.priorTitle: Chancellor of the University of Wisconsin Colleges
leaders.nextRole: Retired; Chancellor Emeritus; remained on the A&T faculty
leaders.notes: Eighth chancellor, serving September 1981 to June 1999; guided A&T to national prominence in engineering and technology, awarded its first engineering Ph.D.s and completed more than $50 million in construction.

leaders.nextRole: Senior Vice President for Programs and Research, American Council on Education
leaders.notes: Ninth chancellor, July 1999 to May 2006; left for the American Council on Education. Died in 2021 at age 72.

leaders.priorTitle: Ethics/leadership consultant; former President of the North Carolina Community College System
leaders.notes: Appointed interim chancellor June 2006 amid a financial-management crisis at A&T. Previously the first African American to lead the North Carolina Community College System; afterward returned to Fayetteville State as interim chancellor.

leaders.nextRole: Interim President, Southern Connecticut State University
leaders.notes: Eleventh chancellor, beginning July 1, 2007; resigned in 2009 citing personal and family reasons. Later a social work professor at the University of Saint Joseph in Connecticut.

leaders.priorTitle: Senior Vice President for Academic Affairs, UNC System (previously Chancellor of Winston-Salem State University)
leaders.notes: Twelfth chancellor, June 2009 to 2024; an A&T alumnus and former A&T dean of engineering. His 15-year transformative tenure grew A&T into the nation's largest HBCU. An engineering research complex is named for him.

leaders.priorTitle: Vice Chancellor for STEM Research and Innovation (formerly Dean of the Swanson School of Engineering)
leaders.notes: Thirteenth chancellor; elected by the UNC Board of Governors June 21, 2024 and began August 15, 2024. Previously dean of Pitt's Swanson School of Engineering (2018-2022) and, earlier, civil engineering chair at Clemson University.

leaders.nextRole: Retired; President Emeritus; returned to the NIU economics faculty
leaders.notes: Tenth president; an economist who rose internally from provost. Over 14 years he established the College of Engineering and Engineering Technology and added more than a dozen academic programs, including several Ph.D. programs.
Eleventh president, June 2000 to June 2013; under him NIU joined the Association of Public and Land-grant Universities and reached the highest Carnegie research classification.

leaders.nextRole: Resigned amid a hiring-classification controversy; returned to NIU as a tenured faculty member
leaders.notes: Twelfth president, effective July 1, 2013; announced his resignation in June 2017 following a state report on improper hiring practices. Led NIU through a period of budget distress and the Illinois budget impasse.

Thirteenth president and first woman to lead NIU. Served as acting president from July 1, 2017 and was appointed permanent president by the Board of Trustees September 23, 2018. On March 19, 2026 she announced she will retire by June 2028; she remains the sitting president.
